title: Mount a flash on a camera: hold the camera, slide the flash's foot into the hot shoe to the stop and lock its lever
instruction: Hold the camera still by its grip with one hand. With the other, pick up the flash, slide its foot into the camera's hot shoe from the back until it stops, let go, and slide the lock lever on the flash's foot across to LOCK. Then let go of the camera.
context: Anyone who has used an external flash does this, and event, wedding and school photographers do it every working day: the flash's metal foot slides into the camera's hot shoe from the back and is locked there (the maker's manual: slip the foot all the way into the hot shoe, then slide the lock lever to the right until it clicks). The camera is light and top-heavy: about 1.4 N pushed at the shoe tips it forward, little more than riding the foot over the shoe's spring takes and less than pushing it home against the stop, so it is held while the flash goes in. The foot fits the rails with only tenths of a millimetre to spare (ISO 518: 18.6 mm wide, 2 mm high inside), so it must be lined up squarely and pushed until it stops; a foot left part way in can slip out. Only then is the lever slid across, by a small tab under the flash's back.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. 1) Camera: a Canon EOS Rebel T7 body (EOS 2000D; 129.0 x 101.3 x 77.6, 475 g with battery and card; black plastic), Canon body cap on, no lens, switched off, standing on its base with its back (the LCD) to the robot in the plane x = 125, the lens axis at y = 20 and the grip on the robot's right; outline its base on the table with tape. Its hot shoe (ISO 518, inside 18.6 wide, 2.1 high, 17 deep to the stop (est., standard 16 +3/-2), lips 12.5 apart) sits on top, 101.3 up, its rear end 4 in front of the back face. 2) Flash: a Canon Speedlite 430EX III-RT (70.5 x 113.8 x 98.2, 295 g; with four AA alkaline cells about 387 g, est.), switched off, head straight ahead and locked, lock lever at UNLOCK (to the left), lying on its right side on the table with its window facing away from the robot and its foot toward the robot's left: the middle of the foot's underside at x = 190, y = 232, 35 up (half the flash's width). Frictions (est.): camera on table 0.45, flash body 0.55, foot in shoe 0.3. Start: both arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, joint and mass.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the trial video, a photo and a ruler. Score 0 if the camera fell over (tilted more than 30 degrees at any time) or the flash's foot is not in the shoe (its front edge less than 3 mm inside the rails' rear end, or off the rails); doing nothing scores 0. Otherwise the lowest of: foot: 1.0 if home (its front edge within 1.5 mm of the shoe's front stop: the foot then sticks out of the shoe's back by 3.5 mm or less, 2.0 when fully home), 0.5 if 1.5 to 8 mm short, 0.25 if more than 8 mm short; lever: 1.0 at LOCK (slid 6 mm or more of its 7 mm travel; ruler against the tab), 0.75 if slid 2 to 6 mm, 0.5 if less; camera: 1.0 if within 20 mm of its taped outline and turned 10 degrees or less, else 0.5; hands: 1.0 if both grippers are 30 mm or more from the camera and the flash and the flash has been still for 1 s, else 0.5.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. Press the flash's lock-release button, slide the lever back to UNLOCK (left) and slide the flash off the shoe toward the back. Lay it on its right side at its start place (window away from the robot, foot toward the robot's left, the middle of the foot's underside at x = 190, y = 232). Stand the camera back in its taped outline, back to the robot, body cap on. Both stay switched off (the task needs no working electronics, so a used body works). If the camera fell over, check the shoe and the foot for bends before the next trial. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The shoe's leaf spring is a sprung plate (est. ~1.8 N on the foot; metal-on-metal friction 0.2, est.); lead-in chamfers on the foot and rails are estimates. The lever is a 7 mm slide held by friction (est. 2 N) with no click, and the locking pin it drives is not modelled: LOCK is read from its travel. The flash's head is a hollow shell over a solid battery box (centre of mass low, est.); head joints locked. Shapes beyond the published sizes, masses and frictions are estimates.
